description: Reverse stock splits scheduled to take effect within a day-offset window of the current US market day, for companies under a market-cap ceiling. Offsets are days from today on the US market calendar: fromOffset=1, toOffset=1 is tomorrow; fromOffset=1, toOffset=7 is the week ahead. Each row carries the ticker, company name, the exact vendor integers (splitFrom/splitTo), a pre-rendered ratio ("1-for-20"), the effective date, market cap, float in shares, and price. floatShares is on the same split basis as the market cap. floatBasis says what it is: "measured", or "estimate" / "estimate_rebased" (the float ladder's point estimate, moved across this split when it predates it), i.e. an estimate rather than a measurement. floatShares: null means not measured or withheld, not zero and not "no float"; such rows are included (they have a valid market cap) and floatWithheldReason gives the reason. floatUnknownCount counts those null-float rows in the list; it is not a withholding count (withheldCount is). price is on the same split basis as the market cap (null when it cannot be stated on one basis), so it is not comparable with a pre-split price from elsewhere. Rows are splits scheduled as of now, not a guarantee that every split effective in the window is already known: the underlying stock_splits table has no created_at column, so when a row first appeared is unmeasurable, and a split announced later is simply missing. The result is "scheduled as of now", not "all" reverse splits. A scheduled split can also be postponed or cancelled after it is announced. capUnknownCount is a withholding count, not a zero: it counts rows that passed every other filter and were deliberately excluded because Signal8 has no measured market cap for them (typically real OTC microcaps). It does not mean those companies have no dilution, no split or no cap; the cap was not measured, so they cannot be asserted to sit under the stated ceiling, and with capUnknownCount above zero the list is not complete for an "under $Xm" framing. Funds, ETFs and sub-1.5x fractional ratio adjustments are already removed server-side, and the ratio is the vendor's. An empty splits array is a normal, common result: most single weekdays have no sub-cap reverse split scheduled at all. It is not an error, not a failure and not evidence that reverse-split activity has stopped. includeLifecycle=true adds Signal8's SEC-filing lifecycle tracker: top-level lifecycleAvailable, and per row `lifecycle` = the tracked episode (state, ratio, ratioRange, meetingDate, the issuer-stated effectiveDate, effectiveCondition, verification, asOf, sourceUrl). lifecycle: null means no episode tracked, not "no split" and not a contradiction of the calendar row; a row with no lifecycle key could not be matched to an SEC registrant (not measured). lifecycleAvailable: false means the tracker is switched off or unreadable, so the response carries no lifecycle information. verification "provisional" = one source, not cross-checked. Scope: this is the vendor market calendar only. The merged list the Signal8 Reverse Splits page shows (the calendar union the SEC-filing tracker, one row per security, with the stage, approval route, authority terms, source filings and the Approved-no-date / Vote-pending tabs) is a separate cross-company list.

fromOffset.description: Window start as a day offset from the US market day (default 1 = tomorrow). Must be <= toOffset; an inverted window is rejected rather than silently returning an empty list.

includeLifecycle.description: Attach the tracked SEC-filing lifecycle episode to each row (default false). null = no episode tracked, never "no split"; a missing key = not matched to a registrant (not measured).

maxMarketCap.description: Exclusive market-cap ceiling in USD (default 300000000). Rows with NO measured market cap are excluded and counted in capUnknownCount, never assumed to be under the ceiling.

toOffset.description: Window end, inclusive, as a day offset from the US market day (default 1). Use 7 with fromOffset 1 for the week ahead. Send it whenever fromOffset is above 1: it defaults to 1, and a fromOffset beyond toOffset is rejected.

name: get_upcoming_reverse_splits
title: Get Upcoming Reverse Splits
